L0: A measured performance penalty that captures how much worse an agent does on the very first task of a fresh work session compared to its usual level, used to quantify a start-of-session ramp-up cost.
L1: A measured performance penalty capturing how much worse an agent performs on the very first task of a fresh work session than on its typical task, used to quantify a start-of-session ramp-up cost. It arises because at the start of a session the agent has not yet worked out which of its internal tools or retrieval indexes is the authoritative one that actually holds the needed information, so early tasks suffer until it does. It is measured as the gap between the score on that first task and the average score across the whole session, and can be lowered by loading the relevant tool or index facts into session memory before work begins.
L2: A measured performance penalty that captures how much worse an agent performs on the very first task of a fresh work session than on its typical task, used to quantify and track a start-of-session ramp-up cost. It happens because at session start the agent has not yet inferred which of its internal tools or retrieval indexes is the authoritative one that holds the data a task needs, so it must spend early effort figuring that out. It is scored as a point gap: the first task's score subtracted from the mean score across that session (for example 12, 15, or 11 points below the session mean). It applies only to the opening task of a new session, not to later tasks in the same session, and the gap is deliberately kept separate from task difficulty, which was controlled for. The gap can be shrunk by seeding session memory with the relevant tool or index facts upfront. The value is tracked as a quarterly average so periods can be compared, dropping from 15 points one quarter to 11 the next after a session-seeding change.
